comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current student curriculum explicitly establishes a 180-EC, three-year programme: 135 EC in the major when no dedicated minor is selected, 45 EC of optional-course-profile space and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. This reconstruction follows the no-dedicated-minor structure, preserves all 45 EC of genuine open profile space and instantiates each restricted choice neutrally from the current official display order. The four named study routes are flexible groupings that may be combined rather than mutually exclusive formal specialisations; the first-listed Economics direction supplies the three year-three major electives without storing a formal route.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It therefore retains the economics and business core while making quantitative financial and economic analysis the organising emphasis. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme-wide economics, business and empirical core. Direct interests and the official flexible study routes support two further coherent directions: public economics with institutions and inequality, and finance with quantitative analysis. Both produce feasible curricula that are substantively distinct from the closest match and from each other. Management and innovation also remain supportable, but production stops at the maximum of three alternatives.

notes.text: Utrecht provides a fixed economics-and-business core, 45 EC of genuine optional-profile space, flexible thematic study routes and a compulsory 15-EC applied-economics thesis. UCR can build coherent economics/business/data, public-economics/institutions and finance/quantitative pathways, but it does not reproduce the same specialist sequence or compulsory economics thesis.
